text:
jess_support: Customer (acme-markets) reporting sustained 429s and timeouts on Dedicated capacity starting ~08:12 PST. They say traffic spike hit and the pool didn't grow. Can someone triage? :eyes:

anil_eng_platform: Looking at the autoscaler logs now. I see failures during node allocation: 

```
ERROR Allocating instance: quotaExceeded: Quota 'CPUS' exceeded for project 1234567890 in region us-west1

Caused by: googleapi: Error 403: Quota 'CPUS' exceeded, quotaExceeded
```

Also some image pull auth failures for the model container around the same time: `unauthorized: authentication required` — might be two separate problems stacking.

sophia_oncall: Confirmed customer reported a backlog in our request queue (queue length hit 500). They saw 503s and then 429s. We have probe traces showing scaleup attempts at 08:13, 08:14, 08:15 but no new nodes joined.

deploy-bot: [08:15] autoscaler triggered scale-up (desired=10 -> 16) but provider returned failures, instances pending=0.

jess_support: Important: customer on Dedicated with reserved capacity + burst enabled. We expected autoscaler to take them from minReplicas 8 -> 16 for the surge. They said the UI showed "scaling" for 12 minutes.

anil_eng_platform: Repro steps I used:
1) From test client: `hey load-test --rps 250 --model redwood-large --endpoint https://dedicated.acme.redwood/api/generate`
2) Watch autoscaler logs: `kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/autoscaler --since=30m`
3) Check cloud operations: `gcloud compute operations list --project=proj-acme --filter="status=RUNNING"`

I also ran `gcloud compute instances create` and hit the same quota error. So cloud quota is likely the gating issue.

kai_billing: I checked the customer's linked cloud project — their CPU quota in us-west1 is at 92% and there are no recent quota increases. We requested a quota increase yesterday but it hasn't been approved. That would explain the allocation failures.

ryan_cs: Customer says they didn't get notified about quota approaching limits. They expected Redwood Dedicated to have fallback behavior. They're upset because their web app saw degraded UX.

anil_eng_platform: Mitigations:
- Short term: reduce burst target to avoid new instance allocations while we wait for quota increase (set maxBurst to 2).
- Short term: fallback to a smaller model variant that fits in existing nodes (redwood-medium) — can route traffic via smart routing policy.
- Mid term: add a clearer telemetry alert when cloud quota > 80% so we can proactively contact customers or auto-fallback.

sophia_oncall: Also: the image pull auth errors need separate handling. I see `imagePullBackOff` for one of the warm pool init pods with log: `error: failed to fetch token from registry: 401 Unauthorized`. If the warm pool can't pull image the pod stays Pending and doesn't contribute to headroom.

jess_support: Repro steps for registry auth: have a test cluster with the customer's service account creds rotated, then `kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml` (model image from private.artifacts.acme). If auth fails, the pod stays in `Init:ImagePullBackOff`.

anil_eng_platform: Action items:
- kai_billing: push quota increase escalation with cloud support and flag as P1 for acme-markets. (DONE: case #CASE-9876)
- sophia_oncall & eng-platform: add an autoscaler retry log annotation so we can see quota vs other reasons in the UI.
- jess_support: propose customer mitigation: temporarily reduce burst and enable smart-routing to medium model. Offer a credits/billing accommodation if they suffered SLA impact.

kai_billing: Confirmed we put priority escalation. Also verifying service account used for registry pulls — it had an expired key rotated this morning, working with the customer's infra team to re-issue.

ryan_cs: Customer accepted the medium-model fallback but asked for an RCA and timeline for preventing this.

anil_eng_platform: Followups:
- I'll add a quick patch to have the autoscaler detect "quotaExceeded" from provider and trigger immediate fallback routing (small PR).
- We'll add a dashboard tile for "cloud quota headroom" and automated Slack alerts at 80%/90%.

sophia_oncall: Postmortem notes: two correlated failures made impact worse: (1) cloud CPU quota exhausted, (2) registry auth rotation prevented warm pool pre-pulls. Either alone might have been manageable, together they blocked scale-up.

jess_support: Thanks team. I'll update the customer thread with the mitigation and ETA. :thumbsup:
